Operations systems + AI
# Your business has outgrown the way it runs.
We find the manual work, broken handoffs, and disconnected systems costing your team time and money. Then we build the systems that remove them.

01 / The problem
## Growth created more coordination than your systems can handle.
You already bought the software. Growth still created more manual work, more handoffs, and more overhead than it should have. That gap between systems is where the money goes.
None of the decisions that got you here were wrong. Somebody still has to own what happens between the systems. Right now, that's you.
Most operators have already tried a new tool, an ops hire, a process review that lived in a doc for three months. The coordination keeps piling up because those fixes treated symptoms, not the gap between systems where the work actually falls.
01Important information lives in people’s heads, not in a system.
02The CRM can’t be trusted, so people keep side spreadsheets.
03The same information gets entered two or three times.
04Growth keeps creating pressure to hire another coordinator.
05The owner is still involved in decisions that shouldn’t need them.
06Nobody knows which system has the right number.
02 / Why SMB Ops
## Most agencies guess. We diagnose.
Most automation agencies skip the hard question: what's actually costing you money? They go straight to the build instead. We answer that question first, with a structured 20+ section audit and the dollar figures to back it up.
### The diagnosis comes first. The build comes second.
Phase 1 puts a dollar figure on every process gap in your operation. Phase 2 turns the most expensive ones into working automations, built by the same team that found them.
No discovery theater. No scope creep. One diagnosis, one team, one accountable outcome from audit through deployment.
01
We share candid assessments. If a tool in your stack is the bottleneck, the Blueprint will name it, with the evidence to back it up.
02
We're not vendor-agnostic. We're vendor-honest. You'll feel the difference on the first call.
Commodity automation vendor
  * Opens with "we can build anything"
  * Scopes off a 30-minute discovery call
  * Sells you the first idea in the room
  * Bills hourly against moving targets
  * Hands off a Zap and a Loom video
  * Disappears at the first deployment friction


SMB Ops
  * Opens with "let’s see the whole operation first"
  * Two-week audit, fixed fee, complete picture
  * Ranks every opportunity before building one
  * Milestone billing tied to deployed systems
  * Documentation, dashboards, training, retainer
  * Stays on through launch, iteration, and expansion


03 / How it works
## Diagnose. Build. Operate.
Most agencies want to start building immediately. We start by mapping where the manual work, handoffs, and broken systems actually are. Before a single automation gets built.
**01** Phase
2 weeks / fixed fee
### The Blueprint
→ Entry point
A complete map of the manual work, handoffs, and disconnected systems in your operation. You'll know your most expensive process problems before we build anything.
  * →14-day sprint. Fixed scope, fixed fee.
  * →No build work starts until you approve the plan.
  * →If you walk away after delivery, you keep everything.


**02** Phase
6–12 weeks / milestone-based
### The Build
→ Execution
We build what Phase 1 surfaced, in the order it ranked. The highest-cost problems first, not the easiest to build. No scope debates. The diagnosis is the scope.
  * →Delivered in ranked order: highest-ROI work first.
  * →Milestone-based invoicing tied to deployed systems.
  * →Daily updates during builds, so your team always knows what shipped and what's next.


**03** Phase
Ongoing / retainer
### Operate & Expand
→ Compounding
Automations decay. Tools change. Teams evolve. The retainer is how the systems keep compounding instead of quietly rotting for six months before someone notices.
  * →Monitoring, iteration, and expansion on systems we built.
  * →Quarterly re-blueprinting as your ops mature.
  * →First access when new capabilities become worth building.

05 / Engagement models
## Three ways to work with us.
One known problem, several connected problems, or ongoing technical ownership. The Blueprint tells you which one fits.
Model / 01 · One known problem
### Automation projects
You know which workflow hurts. We design and build the fix.
Lead follow-up, onboarding, dispatch, reporting, invoice follow-up.
[Scope the build →](https://www.smb-ops.com/services/automation-projects)

### Operations transformation
Fixing one step will not fix the operation. We redesign the whole system.
Spreadsheets, disconnected tools, inconsistent process, key-person risk.
[Start with Blueprint →](https://www.smb-ops.com/services/operations-transformation)

### Fractional AI & operations
An embedded operator who keeps improving the systems after launch.
A backlog of systems, workflow, and AI work with no internal owner.
[Discuss ownership →](https://www.smb-ops.com/services/fractional-ai-operations)
06 / Fit
## Who this is for. Who it isn't.
Best fit: established teams with recurring workflows, multiple systems, and no internal automation owner.
Good fit
  * →Established, service or operations-heavy company.
  * →Recurring workflows across multiple departments.
  * →Multiple software systems that don’t talk to each other.
  * →No internal automation or engineering owner.
  * →An executive with authority to change how work runs.


Probably not the right fit if
  * ·You need one simple Zap.
  * ·You want AI ideas without a defined business problem.
  * ·You want software built without involving the people who run the process.
  * ·Your business does not yet have repeatable operational volume.
  * ·You want to automate a process nobody is willing to change.


07 / Trust
## You keep the keys.
No black boxes, no permanent dependence. See how we handle access, AI, and handover on the [trust page](https://www.smb-ops.com/trust).
### Documentation
Every build ships with documentation your team can actually use without us.
### Access
Systems run in accounts your business owns, wherever practical.
### AI where it earns it
AI only where it does part of the work. Human review stays wherever judgment or risk requires it.
08 / Next
## Book a discovery call.
Thirty minutes to find out whether your operation has a real leak, and whether a Blueprint is the right way to find it.
### Bring the process that's costing you the most time.
We'll tell you whether it looks like a systems problem, a process problem, or something you shouldn't automate. If we're not the right fix, we'll say so on the call and point you somewhere better.
What the call looks like
01We ask where your operation is losing time and money: specific questions, no pitch deck.
02We tell you honestly what we think your biggest leaks are.
03If we're a fit: scope, timeline, and fixed fee on the same call. If not, we'll say so.
